heading: Application for Undergraduate Information Security Engineer Internship 2027
paragraphs: I am applying for the Information Security Engineer internship at Burgess Hill because I want to learn how security controls are actually designed, documented and improved inside a global enterprise - not only how they are described in a framework. American Express works across identities, endpoints, applications, infrastructure and monitoring at a scale where assurance has to be systematic, and a ten-week programme inside Enterprise Technology Services is the environment in which I would learn fastest.

My MSc in Information Security at Royal Holloway, awarded with Merit, covered Security Management with an ISO 27001 focus, Critical Infrastructure Security, Digital Forensics and Network Security, and I hold CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity. That gives me the grounding this role asks for: network protocols and security fundamentals, identity and access management, data protection, and how regulatory expectations translate into controls a team can be measured against. For your engineers, it means I can be useful from the first week rather than needing the concepts explained from scratch.

The responsibilities in this posting are close to what I already do. As an IT Support Assistant I administer access requests through on-premises Active Directory, confirming approval exists before granting anything and limiting permissions to exactly what was requested with a recorded expiry - identity and access management work, carried out manually and documented every time. I investigate four to five suspicious emails a day, checking sender and link domains for impersonation, and I support fifteen colleagues across fifteen to twenty devices, monitoring server health and maintaining access controls. That is the endpoint, identity and alert-triage side of security operations, and it is where my attention to detail was built.

Documentation and reporting are the part of my current work I would bring most directly. At Co-op, as Person in Charge, I run weekly risk assessments and daily compliance checks against operational controls, maintain the assessment records, document incidents through internal reporting systems, track corrective actions and escalate anything unresolved. I have also developed a phishing-analysis prototype in Python with the Gmail API and an LLM, mapping findings to MITRE ATT&CK so they can be triaged in context, and I keep every result for a human to validate before anything is acted on - the same discipline your team describes for AI-enabled detection and triage. I keep sensitive data local by default, because discretion is not optional in this work.

I am genuinely interested in secure architecture, cloud security and AI-enabled security workflows, and I am at the stage where learning from engineers who do this daily is worth more to me than any title. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background could support your team over the summer.
